name: Ausangate Circuit
why: Four days in the high puna around the 6,384 m ice dome of Ausangate, the great apu of Cusco: glacier lakes, red and ochre ridges, alpaca herds and passes over 5,000 m.
book: Bus from Cusco to Tinqui (about 3 h). Backpackers pay a S/10 trail fee at Tinqui and about S/10 at campsites. Most go with an agency from Cusco or Ocongate with packhorses; alone only if you are an experienced high-altitude backpacker. Taxi Pacchanta-Tinqui about S/40.
water: Streams and lakes all the way, but herds graze up to 5,000 m: treat every source.
dangers: Passes from 4,700 to 5,100 m and nights near -10 °C: spend several days acclimatising in Cusco first.
Snow, hail and rain can come on any afternoon, even in the dry season.
Poorly marked in places, remote, with no rescue service.
Guard dogs at the herders' houses: give them a wide berth.
turnaround: Altitude sickness that does not ease overnight (headache, nausea, exhaustion): go down towards Tinqui or Pacchanta instead of crossing the next pass.

points.name: Tinqui (Tinki)
points.note: Day 1: the village at about 3,800 m, 3 h from Cusco. A dirt road climbs through farmland past Upis village.

points.name: Upis camp
points.note: End of day 1, about 10 km: a herders' outpost with horses, basic toilets and a campsite under Ausangate's north face.

points.name: Laguna Ausangate Cocha camp
points.note: Day 2, 16 km over the Arapa pass (4,700 m), past Pucacocha and the Apacheta pass: camp by a small lake right under the glacier.

points.name: Palomani pass
points.note: Day 3: the highest point of the circuit, about 5,100 m, with stone cairns and views in every direction.

points.name: Campa (Qampa) valley camp
points.note: End of day 3, down the alpaca valley beyond Palomani; next morning the Campa pass (about 5,000 m) above its glaciers.

points.name: Pacchanta
points.note: Day 4: down old stone paths to the hamlet with hot pools and a restaurant; taxi back to Tinqui.
